title: Le chéile, ach ina n-aonar

scene.ga: Tá ceathrar déagóirí ina suí thart ar thábla i gcaife san Iúr, agus tá triúr acu ag amharc síos ar a bhfóin gan focal a rá. Tá an ceathrú duine, cailín ar thaobh na láimhe clé, i ndiaidh a guthán a chur síos, agus tá sí ag amharc amach ar an fhuinneog agus cuma uaigneach uirthi. Ar an bhalla taobh thiar díobh, tá clár dubh agus na focail seo air: 'Níl Wi-Fi anseo: bígí ag caint le chéile!'
scene.en: Four teenagers are sitting around a table in a café in Newry, and three of them are looking down at their phones without saying a word. The fourth, a girl on the left, has just put her phone down, and she is looking out of the window with a lonely look on her face. On the wall behind them is a blackboard with these words on it: 'No Wi-Fi here: talk to each other!'

photo: Four sixth-formers (with consent, faces angled down) at a café table in Newry, three on phones and one gazing out of the window, with a chalkboard sign on the wall behind them (chalk the Irish sign yourself).

model.en: The message is that phones are stealing our time together. I think they arranged to meet up today to share the week's news, but they will probably go home without having any real conversation.

model.en: I have to admit that it happens to us too. Last week, we went to a café in Newry and spent half an hour on Snapchat. If I were in this picture, I would put my phone in my bag and start a conversation with the girl on the left.

model.en: I have to admit that I spend about four hours on it every day, especially on TikTok. I would like to cut that down.

followups.ga: An bhfuil sé drochbhéasach do ghuthán a úsáid nuair atá tú amuigh le do chairde?
followups.en: Is it rude to use your phone when you are out with your friends?

model.ga: Tá, dar liom. Má théann tú amach le do chairde, ba cheart duit éisteacht leo. Ach sin ráite, bíonn sé áisiúil grianghraf a thógáil nó ceol a roinnt uaireanta.
model.en: Yes, in my opinion. If you go out with your friends, you should listen to them. But having said that, it is handy to take a photo or share music sometimes.

followups.ga: An rachfá chuig caife gan Wi-Fi?
followups.en: Would you go to a café without Wi-Fi?

model.ga: Rachainn, cinnte. Dá mbeadh caife mar sin sa tSruthán, rachainn ann le mo chairde Dé Sathairn, mar bheadh orainn caint le chéile.
model.en: I would, definitely. If there were a café like that in Bessbrook, I would go there with my friends on Saturday, because we would have to talk to each other.

followups.ga: Cad é a dhéanfaidh tú le d'am scáileáin a laghdú?

model.ga: Múchfaidh mé na fógraí ar mo ghuthán agus fágfaidh mé é i mo sheomra nuair a bheidh mé ag staidéar. Rachaidh mé amach ag siúl níos minice fosta.
model.en: I will turn off the notifications on my phone and I will leave it in my room when I am studying. I will go out walking more often too.

title: Loch nEathach: ár loch i mbaol
titleEn: Lough Neagh: our lough in danger

scene.ga: Tá cladach Loch nEathach le feiceáil, agus tá an t-uisce tiubh, glas agus salach le halgaí gormghlasa. Chun tosaigh, tá comhartha buí ar chuaille agus na focail seo air: 'Trá druidte: ná téigh isteach san uisce.' Sa chúlra, tá bean ag siúl lena madadh, agus tá sí ag tarraingt an mhadaidh ar shiúl ón uisce.
scene.en: The shore of Lough Neagh can be seen, and the water is thick, green and dirty with blue-green algae. In the foreground, there is a yellow sign on a post with these words on it: 'Beach closed: do not go into the water.' In the background, a woman is walking her dog, and she is pulling the dog away from the water.

photo: A Lough Neagh shore in late summer with green algae at the water's edge and a warning sign in the foreground; add the Irish sign text as a caption.

model.en: Yes, especially about the litter that is left at the side of the road in Bessbrook. But I am hopeful, because more young people are taking an interest in the environment now.

model.en: I would not, not yet anyway. I would go in again if the scientists said it was safe, but I would still be afraid.

title: Camloch abú: spórt an phobail

scene.ga: Tá cluiche camógaíochta faoi lán seoil ar pháirc imeartha i gCamloch, agus tá imreoir ag rith síos an pháirc agus an sliotar ar a camán, agus beirt imreoirí eile sa tóir uirthi. Ar thaobh na láimhe deise, tá slua mór de lucht tacaíochta, idir óg agus aosta, ag béicíl agus ag croitheadh bratach, agus tá meirge crochta acu agus 'Camloch Abú!' scríofa air. Ar an chlár scóir sa chúlra, tá an scór 1-12 le 1-10.
scene.en: A camogie match is in full swing on a pitch in Camlough, and a player is running down the pitch with the sliotar on her hurl and two other players chasing her. On the right, a big crowd of supporters, young and old, are shouting and waving flags, and they have hung up a banner with 'Up Camlough!' written on it. On the scoreboard in the background, the score is 1-12 to 1-10.

photo: A local camogie match in Camlough (with the club's and parents' consent), a player in possession in the centre and supporters with flags and a banner on the right, scoreboard visible behind.

model.en: I play Gaelic football with my local club. I remember a final last year when I scored a point in the last minute: I was overjoyed! If I were on this team, I would be quite nervous, but I would be proud too.

ladder.label: Bunúsach
ladder.ga: Tá cluiche camógaíochta ar siúl. Tá daoine ag amharc air.
ladder.en: A camogie match is on. People are watching it.

ladder.label: Níos fearr
ladder.ga: Tá cluiche camógaíochta [faoi lán seoil] [i gCamloch], [agus] tá [slua mór de lucht tacaíochta] ag amharc air.
ladder.en: A camogie match is [in full swing] [in Camlough], [and] [a big crowd of supporters is] watching it.

ladder.label: Is fearr
ladder.ga: Tá cluiche camógaíochta faoi lán seoil i gCamloch, agus tá slua mór de lucht tacaíochta ag amharc air [agus ag spreagadh a bhfoirne], [mar níl ach dhá chúilín idir an dá fhoireann].
ladder.en: A camogie match is in full swing in Camlough, and a big crowd of supporters is watching it [and urging on their team], [because there are only two points between the two teams].

followups.ga: Cad chuige a bhfuil an CLG chomh tábhachtach sin do phobal beag?
followups.en: Why is the GAA so important to a small community?

model.ga: Is é an club croílár an pharóiste. Tugann sé áit do dhaoine óga le bualadh le chéile agus fanacht aclaí, agus bíonn achan duine ag obair ar son an chlub: na tuismitheoirí, na seanóirí agus na himreoirí óga.
model.en: The club is the heart of the parish. It gives young people a place to meet and stay fit, and everyone works for the club: the parents, the older people and the young players.

followups.ga: An bhfaigheann mná a gcothrom féin sa spórt?
followups.en: Do women get fair treatment in sport?

model.ga: Ní fhaigheann, go fóill. Tá níos mó daoine ag amharc ar chamógaíocht agus ar pheil na mban anois ná riamh, ach ní bhíonn an oiread céanna airgid ná poiblíochta acu is a bhíonn ag na fir. Sílim gur cheart sin a athrú.
model.en: No, not yet. More people are watching camogie and ladies' football now than ever, but they do not get the same amount of money or publicity as the men. I think that should change.

followups.ga: Dá mbeadh an t-am agat, cén spórt úr a thosófá?
followups.en: If you had the time, what new sport would you take up?

model.ga: Dá mbeadh an t-am agam, thosóinn ag imirt camógaíochta, mar tá cairde de mo chuid ar an fhoireann agus bíonn craic mhór acu. Ach leis na scrúduithe AS, níl mórán ama saor agam i mbliana.
model.en: If I had the time, I would start playing camogie, because friends of mine are on the team and they have great fun. But with the AS exams, I do not have much free time this year.

title: Oíche fhuar, croí te
titleEn: A cold night, a warm heart

scene.ga: Tá sé ina oíche fhuar fhliuch ar shráid i lár Bhéal Feirste, agus tá fear ina shuí ar mhála codlata i ndoras siopa atá druidte, agus a chloigeann cromtha agus hata olla air. Tá oibrí deonach, bean óg i seaicéad buí, ag cromadh síos chuige, agus tá sí ag tabhairt babhla anraith the agus ceapaire dó. Ar phíosa cairtchláir in aice leis, tá na focail seo scríofa: 'Tá ocras orm. Go raibh maith agat.'
scene.en: It is a cold, wet night on a street in the centre of Belfast, and a man is sitting on a sleeping bag in the doorway of a closed shop, his head bowed and a woolly hat on him. A volunteer, a young woman in a yellow jacket, is bending down to him, and she is giving him a bowl of hot soup and a sandwich. On a piece of cardboard beside him, these words are written: 'I am hungry. Thank you.'

photo: A staged shot with consenting adults: a man in a doorway at night, face hidden or turned away, and a volunteer in a yellow jacket handing him soup; never photograph a real homeless person.

model.en: In this picture, I see a man sitting in a shop doorway in Belfast. It is night and the street is wet. A young woman is bending down and giving him a bowl of soup.

model.en: I would say the man is cold, tired and hungry, and maybe he is ashamed too. But the young woman looks kind, and I think she is glad that she can help.

model.en: 'I am hungry. Thank you.' is written on a piece of cardboard. It is a simple message, but it shows that he depends on the kindness of other people.

model.en: We cannot be sure, but maybe he lost his job or his home, or he had mental health problems. The message is that anyone can become homeless, and that we can all help. Tonight, at least, he will have a hot meal.

model.ga: Feicim, faraor. Roimh an Nollaig, chuaigh mé isteach go Béal Feirste le mo mham agus cheannaigh muid cupán tae agus ceapaire d'fhear a bhí ina shuí taobh amuigh de stáisiún na traenach. Dá mbeadh an t-am agam, ghlacfainn páirt in obair dheonach mar seo.
model.en: I do, unfortunately. Before Christmas, I went into Belfast with my mum and we bought a cup of tea and a sandwich for a man who was sitting outside the train station. If I had the time, I would take part in voluntary work like this.

ladder.label: Bunúsach
ladder.ga: Tá fear ina shuí ar an tsráid. Tá bean ag tabhairt bia dó.
ladder.en: A man is sitting on the street. A woman is giving him food.

ladder.label: Níos fearr
ladder.ga: Tá fear [gan dídean] ina shuí [i ndoras siopa] ar an tsráid, [agus] tá bean ag tabhairt bia [te] dó.
ladder.en: A [homeless] man is sitting [in a shop doorway] on the street, [and] a woman is giving him [hot] food.

ladder.label: Is fearr
ladder.ga: Tá fear gan dídean ina shuí i ndoras siopa ar an tsráid [ar oíche fhuar fhliuch], agus tá [oibrí deonach] ag tabhairt bia te dó, [rud a léiríonn go bhfuil cineáltas ar an tsaol go fóill].
ladder.en: A homeless man is sitting in a shop doorway on the street [on a cold, wet night], and [a volunteer] is giving him hot food, [which shows that there is still kindness in the world].

followups.ga: Cad chuige a mbíonn daoine gan dídean, dar leat?
followups.en: Why do people become homeless, in your opinion?

model.ga: Is iomaí cúis atá leis an fhadhb: andúil, fadhbanna sláinte intinne, briseadh sa teaghlach, agus cíos atá ródhaor. Ní ar an duine féin a bhíonn an locht i gcónaí.
model.en: There are many causes of the problem: addiction, mental health problems, family breakdown, and rent that is too expensive. It is not always the person's own fault.

followups.ga: Cé air a bhfuil an fhreagracht cuidiú leo?
followups.en: Whose responsibility is it to help them?

model.ga: Sílim gur cheart don Rialtas níos mó tithe sóisialta a thógáil agus tuilleadh airgid a chur ar fáil do sheirbhísí sláinte intinne. Ach sin ráite, thig linn uilig cuidiú, fiú le focal cineálta.
model.en: I think the government should build more social housing and provide more money for mental health services. But having said that, we can all help, even with a kind word.

followups.ga: An dtugann tú airgead do dhaoine a bhíonn ag iarraidh déirce?
followups.en: Do you give money to people who are begging?

model.ga: Uaireanta tugaim, ach is fearr liom bia nó deoch the a cheannach dóibh. Sílim go bhfuil sé tábhachtach labhairt leo fosta, mar is minic a bhíonn uaigneas orthu.
model.en: Sometimes I do, but I prefer to buy them food or a hot drink. I think it is important to talk to them too, because they are often lonely.

followups.ga: Dá mbeadh an chumhacht agat, cad é a dhéanfá leis an fhadhb a réiteach?
followups.en: If you had the power, what would you do to solve the problem?

model.ga: Dá mbeadh an chumhacht agam, thógfainn tithe beaga saora do dhaoine óga, agus chuirfinn áit shlán le codladh ar fáil d'achan duine a bhfuil sé de dhíth air, i mBéal Feirste, san Iúr agus in Ard Mhacha.
model.en: If I had the power, I would build small, cheap homes for young people, and I would provide a safe place to sleep for everyone who needs it, in Belfast, Newry and Armagh.

title: Am dinnéir nó am cluichíochta?

scene.ga: Tá teaghlach ina suí thart ar thábla na cistine ag am dinnéir, agus tá gal ag éirí ó phláta mór spaghetti i lár an tábla. Tá an mháthair ag caint agus an deartháir beag ag gáire, ach tá déagóir ar thaobh na láimhe clé ag imirt cluiche ar a chonsól láimhe agus cluasáin air, agus tá cuma chrosta ar a athair. Ar an chuisneoir sa chúlra, tá maighnéad agus na focail seo air: 'Gan fóin ag an tábla!'
scene.en: A family is sitting around the kitchen table at dinner time, and steam is rising from a big plate of spaghetti in the middle of the table. The mother is talking and the little brother is laughing, but a teenager on the left is playing a game on his handheld console, with headphones on, and his father looks cross. On the fridge in the background, there is a magnet with these words on it: 'No phones at the table!'

photo: A staged family dinner at a kitchen table (consenting family or staff volunteers), a teenager on a handheld console with headphones, a cross-looking parent, and a fridge magnet sign behind.

model.en: In this picture, I see a family eating dinner together in the kitchen. The mother is talking and the little brother is laughing, but on the left a teenager is playing a game on his console.

model.en: I think the father will take the console from him and put it in the drawer until dinner is over. The message is that family time is precious, and that we have to put technology aside sometimes.

model.en: We eat together every Sunday, and nobody is allowed to bring a phone to the table. Last year, I was hooked on an online game and we had arguments about it. If I were a parent, I would have the same rule.

ladder.en: A family is eating dinner in the kitchen, and a boy is playing a game on his console instead of talking, [although the house rule is stuck to the fridge in front of him].

followups.ga: An bhfuil sé tábhachtach go n-itheann teaghlaigh le chéile?
followups.en: Is it important that families eat together?

model.ga: Tá, cinnte. Is é am an dinnéir an t-aon am sa lá a mbíonn muid uilig le chéile, agus bíonn deis againn labhairt faoin lá.
model.en: Yes, definitely. Dinner time is the only time in the day when we are all together, and we have a chance to talk about the day.

followups.ga: An mbíonn argóintí agaibh sa bhaile faoin teicneolaíocht?
followups.en: Do you have arguments at home about technology?

model.ga: Bíonn, go minic! Síleann mo thuismitheoirí go gcaithim an iomarca ama ar mo ghuthán, agus b'fhéidir go bhfuil an ceart acu. Ach bíonn m'athair féin ag amharc ar an nuacht ar a ghuthán ag an tábla!
model.en: Yes, often! My parents think I spend too much time on my phone, and maybe they are right. But my dad himself looks at the news on his phone at the table!

followups.ga: Cad é mar a bheidh saol an teaghlaigh i gceann fiche bliain, dar leat?
followups.en: What will family life be like in twenty years, do you think?

model.ga: Is dóigh liom go mbeidh níos mó scáileán sa teach, agus b'fhéidir go mbeidh róbait ag cócaireacht dúinn! Ach tá súil agam go mbeidh am dinnéir ann go fóill.
model.en: I think there will be more screens in the house, and maybe robots will be cooking for us! But I hope there will still be a dinner time.

followups.ga: Dá mbeadh cosc ar ghutháin agus ar chonsóil i do theach ar feadh seachtaine, cad é a dhéanfá?
followups.en: If phones and consoles were banned in your house for a week, what would you do?

model.ga: Bheadh sé doiligh ar dtús, ach rachainn amach ag siúl le mo mhadadh agus léifinn leabhar. B'fhéidir go n-imreodh muid / go n-imreoimis cluichí cláir mar theaghlach fosta.
model.en: It would be hard at first, but I would go out walking with my dog and I would read a book. Maybe we would play board games as a family too.

title: Ár sliabh, ár bhfreagracht

scene.ga: Tá grúpa daltaí i gcótaí báistí ag siúl suas cosán ar Shliabh gCuillinn, agus lámhainní orthu agus málaí bruscair ina lámha. Chun tosaigh, tá buachaill ag síneadh isteach san fhraoch le buidéal plaisteach a phiocadh suas, agus sa chúlra tá na páirceanna glasa le feiceáil thíos fúthu sa cheo. Ag tús an chosáin, tá comhartha adhmaid agus na focail seo air: 'Ná fág i do dhiaidh ach lorg coise.'
scene.en: A group of pupils in raincoats is walking up a path on Slieve Gullion, with gloves on and bin bags in their hands. In the foreground, a boy is reaching into the heather to pick up a plastic bottle, and in the background the green fields can be seen below them in the mist. At the start of the path, there is a wooden sign with these words on it: 'Leave nothing behind but a footprint.'

model.ga: Sa phictiúr seo, feicim grúpa daltaí ag bailiú bruscair ar Shliabh gCuillinn. Tá lámhainní orthu agus málaí bruscair ina lámha. Chun tosaigh, tá buachaill ag síneadh isteach san fhraoch le buidéal a phiocadh suas.
model.en: In this picture, I see a group of pupils collecting litter on Slieve Gullion. They have gloves on and bin bags in their hands. In the foreground, a boy is reaching into the heather to pick up a bottle.

fingers.q: Cad é do bharúil faoin rud a fheiceann tú?
fingers.qEn: What do you think of what you see?

frames.ga: Is pictiúr dearfach é, dar liom, mar...
frames.en: It is a positive picture, in my opinion, because...

frames.ga: Tá cuma thuirseach orthu, ach...
frames.en: They look tired, but...

frames.ga: Is léir go bhfuil bród orthu as...
frames.en: It is clear that they are proud of...

frames.ga: Cuireann sé fearg orm go bhfágann daoine bruscar...
frames.en: It makes me angry that people leave litter...

model.ga: Is pictiúr dearfach é, dar liom, mar tá daoine óga ag déanamh rud éigin maith don cheantar. Tá cuma thuirseach fhliuch orthu, ach is léir go bhfuil bród orthu as a gcuid oibre.
model.en: It is a positive picture, in my opinion, because young people are doing something good for the area. They look tired and wet, but it is clear that they are proud of their work.

fingers.q: Cad é atá scríofa ar an chomhartha?
fingers.qEn: What is written on the sign?

frames.ga: Tá '...' scríofa ar an chomhartha
frames.en: '...' is written on the sign

frames.ga: Ciallaíonn sé sin gur cheart do shiúlóirí...
frames.en: That means that walkers should...

frames.ga: a gcuid bruscair a thabhairt leo abhaile
frames.en: to take their litter home with them

frames.ga: Is teachtaireacht láidir í
frames.en: It is a strong message

model.ga: Tá 'Ná fág i do dhiaidh ach lorg coise' scríofa ar an chomhartha. Ciallaíonn sé sin gur cheart do shiúlóirí a gcuid bruscair uilig a thabhairt leo abhaile.
model.en: 'Leave nothing behind but a footprint' is written on the sign. That means that walkers should take all their litter home with them.

fingers.q: Cad é a tharla ar an tsliabh roimhe seo, dar leat? Cén teachtaireacht atá ann?
fingers.qEn: What happened on the mountain before this, do you think? What is the message?

frames.ga: Is dóigh liom gur fhág cuairteoirí...
frames.en: I think visitors left...

frames.ga: i rith an tsamhraidh
frames.en: during the summer

frames.ga: Shocraigh an scoil an sliabh a ghlanadh
frames.en: The school decided to clean the mountain

frames.ga: Is í an teachtaireacht atá ann gur linne uilig...
frames.en: The message is that ... belongs to us all

model.ga: Is dóigh liom gur fhág cuairteoirí a gcuid bruscair ina ndiaidh i rith an tsamhraidh, agus gur shocraigh an scoil an sliabh a ghlanadh. Is í an teachtaireacht atá ann gur linne uilig an timpeallacht, agus gur orainne atá an fhreagracht aire a thabhairt di.
model.en: I think visitors left their litter behind them during the summer, and the school decided to clean up the mountain. The message is that the environment belongs to us all, and that it is our responsibility to look after it.

fingers.q: An ndearna tú a leithéid riamh? Cad é do bharúil féin?
fingers.qEn: Have you ever done anything like this? What is your own opinion?

frames.ga: Ghlac mé páirt i...
frames.en: I took part in...

frames.ga: Bhailigh muid ... in aon mhaidin amháin
frames.en: We collected ... in one single morning

frames.ga: I mo thaithí féin, ...
frames.en: In my own experience, ...

frames.ga: Dá mbeadh níos mó ... ann, sílim go mbeadh...
frames.en: If there were more ..., I think there would be...

model.ga: Rinne. Ghlac mé páirt i nglanadh an bhaile sa tSruthán i mBliain 11, agus bhailigh muid fiche mála bruscair in aon mhaidin amháin. Dá mbeadh níos mó boscaí bruscair ar an tsliabh, sílim go mbeadh níos lú bruscair ann.
model.en: I have. I took part in a clean-up of the village in Bessbrook in Year 11, and we collected twenty bags of litter in one single morning. If there were more bins on the mountain, I think there would be less litter there.

ladder.label: Bunúsach
ladder.ga: Tá daltaí ar an tsliabh. Tá siad ag bailiú bruscair.
ladder.en: Pupils are on the mountain. They are collecting litter.

ladder.label: Níos fearr
ladder.ga: Tá daltaí [scoile] ar [Shliabh gCuillinn], [agus] tá siad ag bailiú bruscair [i málaí dubha].
ladder.en: [School] pupils are on [Slieve Gullion], [and] they are collecting litter [in black bags].

ladder.label: Is fearr
ladder.ga: Tá daltaí scoile ar Shliabh gCuillinn, agus tá siad ag bailiú bruscair i málaí dubha [le go mbeidh an sliabh glan do chách], [rud a léiríonn go bhfuil meas acu ar a gceantar].
ladder.en: School pupils are on Slieve Gullion, and they are collecting litter in black bags [so that the mountain will be clean for everyone], [which shows that they respect their area].

followups.ga: An bhfuil fadhb bruscair i do cheantar féin?
followups.en: Is there a litter problem in your own area?

model.ga: Tá, go háirithe cois an bhóthair idir an Sruthán agus an tIúr. Caitheann daoine cannaí agus cupáin chaife amach as fuinneoga a gcarranna, rud atá náireach.
model.en: Yes, especially beside the road between Bessbrook and Newry. People throw cans and coffee cups out of their car windows, which is shameful.

followups.ga: Cé air a bhfuil an fhreagracht an ceantar a choinneáil glan?
followups.en: Whose responsibility is it to keep the area clean?

model.ga: Ar achan duine againn. Ba cheart don chomhairle níos mó boscaí bruscair a chur ar fáil, ach ag deireadh an lae, is é an duine a chaitheann an bruscar atá ciontach.
model.en: It is on every one of us. The council should provide more bins, but at the end of the day, the person who throws the litter is the one to blame.

followups.ga: Cad é a dhéanfaidh do scoil ar son na timpeallachta i mbliana?
followups.en: What will your school do for the environment this year?

model.ga: Beidh lá glantacháin eile againn san earrach, agus tá an Coiste Glas ag iarraidh fáil réidh le plaisteach aon úsáide sa cheaintín. Glacfaidh mé páirt ann, cinnte.
model.en: We will have another clean-up day in the spring, and the Eco Committee wants to get rid of single-use plastic in the canteen. I will take part in it, definitely.

followups.ga: Dá mbeifeá i do chomhairleoir, cad é a dhéanfá leis an tsliabh a chosaint?
followups.en: If you were a councillor, what would you do to protect the mountain?

model.ga: Dá mbeinn i mo chomhairleoir, chuirfinn níos mó boscaí bruscair ag tús na gcosán, agus ghearrfainn fíneáil mhór ar dhaoine a fhágann bruscar ina ndiaidh.
model.en: If I were a councillor, I would put more bins at the start of the paths, and I would give a big fine to people who leave litter behind them.
